visual_action: A nighttime fireworks display with predominantly pink, red, and purple explosions illuminates the sky over a large, lit monument with fountains, which appears to be the World War II Memorial in Washington D.C. In the foreground, silhouettes of people are seen watching the show; one person holds up a phone to record the event.

cast.name: United States of America
cast.evidence: The on-screen text refers to "the greatest country on Earth" in a video posted by the official White House account, clearly implying the United States.

on_screen_text.text: The greatest fireworks show for the greatest country on Earth

spoken_summary: There is no dialogue. The audio consists of lyrics from a song: "Hot summer nights, mid July, when you and I were forever wild... Will you still love me when I'm no longer young and beautiful?"
audio_music: The video is set to a slow, cinematic, and nostalgic-sounding pop song, identified as "Young And Beautiful" by Lana Del Rey, which plays throughout the clip.
editing_pacing: The video consists of a single, static shot focused on the fireworks display over the monument, with no cuts or dynamic camera movements.
cultural_references: The song "Young and Beautiful" by musician Lana Del Rey is used as the soundtrack.
central_claim: The United States is the greatest country on Earth, as demonstrated by its spectacular national celebrations like this fireworks show.
intended_effect: To evoke feelings of patriotism, awe, and deep affection for the country.
